battler_words:card.comment: The BtlrCard, BN6's own: its key item and the flags BN6's HeelNavi sets as he sells it (the card, Mettaur's and Gunner's data), and his rules

battler_words:offer.comment: The pair, the stake and the question, then the stake taken, into the script under way: the box opened (`first`), and the pot's rule in a line where the card's chat has not said it all

battler_words:pot.comment: The pot given, as BN6 gives zenny

battler_words:series_won.comment: The series won: the pot, and a first win's prize

battler_words:won.comment: A win short of the series' end: the pot, the next pair, and the choice

board_words:compressed_words.comment: A program's compression code entered the first time in any run (issue #50; `about` its NaviCust words, "Name: ..."): Dad's lab compresses it in every dive after, and its code is in his mail

board_words:off_board_words.comment: MegaMan's word for a program left off the board, once a layer (NULL: none to say), where it fits beside those on it; how to place it, turn it or make room is the player's, as in BN6 (the voice sweep, 19 October 2026: docs/voice/sweep/net.md).

board_words:reg_words.comment: MegaMan's words on Reg memory (issue #51), `reg` MB of it: the first RegUp in any run; a RegUp after that; and the TagChip system, for a profile whose Chaud's clearance came before it did. What a Regular Chip and a TagChip are, and their buttons, are BN6's own, unsaid (the voice sweep, docs/voice/sweep/net.md).

briefing_words:arena_ahead.comment: The last stop's first box: whose arena is just ahead (a super boss's sensed until they have met: docs/game/bosses/super-bosses.md); its length

briefing_words:first_words.comment: L's first words on a layer: where they are and what guards it, appended to `buf` at `k`; the new length.

briefing_words:goal_words.comment: L's last words, the way on, appended to `buf` at `k`; the new length: along the floor where MegaMan can walk it (the arrow's way); where the walk sets off well away from where the goal lies, where it lies, which holds still as the walk winds; after the heal's words (`to_heal`, the arrow leading there first), where the goal lies: "the way on" read as the arrow's, which led to the heal, and its first leg is from here, not from the heal (session 62).

briefing_words:guardian_words.comment: MegaMan's words on the layer's guardian, on arriving: who he is and how he fights once they have fought him, in any run (the tip, strategy, is kept here for BN5's guardians and the super bosses, whom no mail of Dad's covers; noted for the BBS, docs/voice/sweep/net.md); before that only hearsay or a strong signal, as naming him would spend the first fight's discovery (and how could he know?). The yellow panels and EraseCross's bug are BN6's own, unsaid (the voice sweep). Appended to `buf` at `k`; the new length.

briefing_words:heal_note.comment: L's word on a heal while MegaMan is hurt, appended to `buf` at `k`; the new length: which way the Recovery Mr. Prog is, the arrow's way while he is hurt (goal_way), else the Net Dealer, who always has a MiniEnrg (it was on no map yet, and never found: a playtester at 90 of 240 ran to the exit past the dealer, then a dozen moves back).

briefing_words:here_names.comment: What L names among what is here: the services, then what the map marks violet, then an official gate; their number. What each is, the piece itself says at A (the map's lessons went in the voice sweep, docs/voice/sweep/net.md; profile.marks_taught keeps what it had).

briefing_words:lock_words.comment: Where lock `lock` stands while it is shut, for L's words after the data he senses behind it, as his words on ProtoMan and the heal point (a playtester heard "behind the security cube", was told its P-Code by a navi and never found the cube, session 64): appended to `buf` at `k`, the new length.

briefing_words:more_words.comment: L's second words on a layer: the area's battlefields and viruses, the ScrtData carried, then what is here in one breath (a playtester paged eight boxes on arriving in act 3): the services (the map marks a trader as a shop, and L had said nothing of one), the map's violet marks, in full until explained (a playtester stood beside one and never found out what it was), named after that, the set pieces, the rival, a program off the board and the map's tip; appended to `buf` at `k`, the new length.

briefing_words:off_board_note.comment: L's word on a program left off the board, appended to `buf` at `k`; the new length. Said on every layer until placed, unless MegaMan has said it on this layer already (a playtester heard it on CONTINUE, then again in L's first words); not for one that cannot fit beside the others, nor how to turn one or make room, BN6's own (the voice sweep, docs/voice/sweep/net.md).

briefing_words:piece_talk.comment: What each is called among what MegaMan senses. What it is and what opens it are BN6's own, or said by the piece itself at A (a lesson a profile's first time went in the voice sweep, docs/voice/sweep/net.md; profile.pieces_taught keeps what it had).

briefing_words:prize_note.comment: The data MegaMan senses but has not seen, said where it lies (two at most), and the locks it is behind, appended to `buf` at `k`; the new length.

briefing_words:prize_where.comment: Where a set piece keeps Mystery Data k, as L says it ("behind the security cube"), or NULL: the counters count data MegaMan senses there, and a playtester's read 0/1 with nothing in sight and no word of where (session 63). The lock it is behind in *lock (layer.block[]), -1 none.

briefing_words:sense_words.comment: What MegaMan senses on the layer (`here`, n of them), appended to `buf` at `k`, then the rival, whose call has said why (docs/game/rival.md), apart: in the list, "ProtoMan, waiting for our duel and an official gate" read as waiting for the gate too (a playtester's). His race named a race, as Chaud's call does: "our duel" read as a fight a playtester skipped (session 62). The new length.

briefing_words:service_where.comment: (where a service lies from MegaMan, as L and the map give it, and how far the walk there is: "right here,to the left", "to the lower right", "a long way back,straight up"; where the walk sets off another way, that it winds: the walk's first step, "up and to the right", named a heal that L and the map put up and to the left)

briefing_words:status_words.comment: What MegaMan says when L is pressed: where they are, what is ahead.

dark_words:dark_base_words.comment: A DarkChip that ran as its base chip for want of a BugFrag, into `out`

dark_words:dark_bn5_does.header: What a DarkChip played by BN5's rule does, for a flame's words (pages apart by '|'), "" where its words say none: DarkPlus's `plus` more for the next attack chip, DarkInvs's (`invs`) ten seconds of the darkness fighting for him, unseen (BN5's 600 frames; the owner's calls of 13 October 2026)

dark_words:dark_price_words.comment: A DarkChip's price, `lost` max HP (dark_price): the first BN6 battle's, its bug gone (what it burned, its flame has said); the session's first; one more

duel_words:duel_call_words.comment: Chaud's call on a duel layer (docs/game/rival.md): the record, ProtoMan's time and the term, what a win opens, and Lan's answer.

duel_words:verdict_result.comment: Chaud's first words on a duel's end, with both times as the results screen shows them: the netbattle, a win, a hit taken, a time too slow.

duel_words:verdict_words.comment: Chaud's words on a duel's end (duel_verdict), with both times as the results screen shows them, into `out` (`size` bytes)

emote_strip_text:strip_text_favourites.header: the keys' hints: the favourites' box's, the palette's

emote_strip_text:strip_text_kept.header: a favourite just kept: "ON L+UP" for way 0-3

gate_words:gate_end_words.header: How a visit ended (online_visit.h), said at the gate after it, and whose face says it (FACE_*); NULL nothing to say.

gate_words:gate_keeper_official.header: ... and his answers: the gate set to the official Square; B.

gate_words:gate_keeper_set.header: ... the gate set to another server's address; the name `name` saved.

gate_words:gate_question.header: MegaMan's question on the gate, the way known.

gate_words:gate_save_failed.header: The checkpoint before a visit not written: MegaMan stays (the game's own note says why, never a character: docs/voice/rules.md, What nobody says).

guardian_lines:answer.comment: MegaMan answers now and then, never over a first meeting (after a loss the record in it: "I'm ready this time!" before every rematch read as a loop to a playtester two down against CircusMan).

guardian_lines:first_sight.comment: How MegaMan and Lan take guardian `navi`, `name`, at the first meeting: a friend's copy, a foe's, or a Navi of the older net (BN5's, copied with it)

guardian_lines:greeting.comment: What the guardian says on meeting MegaMan: a first meeting's line, his revenge after a win, a stronger version's, respect after three losses, else a rematch's.

guardian_lines:guardian_netbattle_terms.comment: (MegaMan's battle data on him is Dad's mail's: recited here before the choice, it was MegaMan coaching, docs/voice/rules.md, What nobody says)

guardian_lines:guardian_rumor.comment: (a first meeting's hint: the net's gossip, which lives in that world and could know something, as the Net Dealer's "word is" does; a name's worth of insight, the moves left for the fight to show, and EraseMan's danger said as a danger: an erase at low HP had come with no word)

guardian_lines:guardian_soul_words.comment: MegaMan on an older net guardian's Soul (docs/game/meta/souls.md), won from `navi`, of chip kind `kind` (BN5_CHIP_KIND, 0-11): one held already (`held`); else that it serves every battle, the whole of it the first time, `chip` one of the run's chips of its kind ("" none); and, where `form` (once a profile), that a Soul and a Cross are not worn together

guardian_lines:lines.comment: What each says: meeting MegaMan the first time, again after losing to him, after beating him, as a stronger version, and when deleted. They are the Nest's copies (docs/game/bosses/), built from every battle the net has seen: they remember.

guardian_lines:replies.comment: MegaMan's answer, for the lines that give him one ("I'm ready this time!" only after a loss: a playtester 3-0 against SpoutMan heard it)

guardian_lines:respect.comment: Rematches after many of MegaMan's wins: grudging respect.

home_words:area_feel.comment: What MegaMan reads of an area through a link he has not taken: its data, never its name (docs/game/meta/what-megaman-knows.md)

home_words:clock_feel.comment: how far the Net's clock has run, in MegaMan's words

home_words:home_aster_words.header: L's words in AsterLand: where its counter takes orders and sells SubChips, then `words`.

home_words:home_back_portal_words.header: MegaMan beside an older portal (docs/world/home/going-back.md): where it leads (an area won, so named) and its price on the Net's clock, all of it until `taught`.

home_words:home_back_question.header: MegaMan's question before a trip back (talk_ask's).

home_words:home_back_words.header: Home again from a trip back, the Net's clock at `clock`.

home_words:home_courier_words.header: The courier in Lan's HP (docs/world/home/lans-hp.md, piece 2), the most valuable first, a box each: the pay waiting with asker `reward` (jobs.h, -1 none), else the places of the requests posted (bit k asker k), new after an act, simply up at the run's first visit (`first`), and what AsterLand's SubChip seller has in stock: `unlockers` Unlockers, RushFood, a WWW-ID. "" for none.

home_words:home_door_words.header: L's words in Lan's house `words`, then where its front door is (`door` from Lan, way_to's word).

home_words:home_errands_words.header: L's words at home `words`, then once a visit what it holds besides the way on: `requests` posted (none held), an order `order` AsterLand can still make that the zenny held pays for, and which way AsterLand is (`aster`, way_to's word; NULL unsaid).

home_words:home_hp_status.header: L in Lan's HP: the pink pad `way` from MegaMan, and how far the Net's clock has run (`clock` its notches); R, BN6's jack-out, unsaid (docs/voice/rules.md, What nobody says).

home_words:home_hp_words.header: MegaMan in Lan's HP the run's first time there: what it is, or, to a profile `taught` that, a word.

home_words:home_on_question.header: ... and before a way on through a link.

home_words:home_port_words.header: MegaMan at a portal (docs/world/home/): what he reads through the link of area `biome` (its data, never its name: he has not been there) and of `navi` its guardian (his signal named where MegaMan has battled him); `dark` the dark way into the Undernet, `sealed` that way still shut; `board` its act's dark layer that way, `route` the way a special route found on a dark layer opened.

home_words:home_words.header: Their words on arriving in Lan's HP, `beaten` the guardian just deleted (NULL unknown), the run at the next act's first layer; its ways open, `ports[0..ways)` the portals' names ("pink pad"), `sealed` where a dark way's stands shut (NULL none), and `route` the portal of a special route's way (docs/game/liberation/special-routes.md; -1 none).

job_words:hand_over.comment: a chip handed over: chip c of the talk's, taken from the Pack, then the pay

job_words:job_board_words.header: What AsterLand's request board reads (A at it): the board's post.

job_words:job_done_words.header: MegaMan in the Net: a request done, a vow broken, the vow's reminder.

job_words:pay_name.comment: the pay as a thing: "600 Zenny", "7 BugFrags", "Cannon A", "2 HPMemory"

launcher_text:words.comment: (in LauncherWord's order, one a line, its name beside it)

layer_words:dealer_keys.comment: (the keys he stocks, said: what each opens and where, issues #41, #14, #47)

layer_words:dealer_rush.comment: (Rush's gap, and how wide: as many RushFood as its panels call him, BN6's own rule, unsaid; a playtester would have bought one of three, session 64, and the width says how many)

layer_words:dealer_word.comment: The Net Dealer's word on the act's guardian, `navi`, by his list (`stock`, n of them): the element he can't stand (of either wheel: TenguMan's Sword, issue #39) and the pick of it, first on the list; for one weak to none, the hardest hit, and the viruses' weakness besides where the list has a chip of it (an element-less guardian's act is answered for its viruses). ElementMan's element changes as he fights, so none answers him for long. One tip, a seller's: how a chip lands and a Navi's armor are strategy, the BBS's (the voice sweep, docs/voice/sweep/net.md).

layer_words:dealer_words.comment: The Net Dealer's greeting and its word on the act's guardian and the keys he stocks; his line when he is visited again, and sold out

layer_words:duel_terms.comment: ProtoMan's terms for a race (docs/game/rival.md), into `terms`: the time to beat (`frames`), as the results screen shows a DeleteTime (seconds and hundredths, cut), and the rung's rule; the squad (`foes` viruses) and the stake said before the choice (a playtester took it at 100 HP, nothing saying it was a real fight; and the two are old rivals, not strangers); the first duel (`met` none before) says who he is. To heal first goes unsaid, and the stake is noted (the voice sweep, docs/voice/sweep/net.md).

layer_words:hinter_words.comment: A bystander's hint at an invisible path (issue #46)

layer_words:netbattle_later_words.comment: ProtoMan's words where his netbattle waits for a later act: where, as the net goes ("the third act" was the game's word, not his).
layer_words:netbattle_later_words.header: ProtoMan's word where his netbattle waits for a later act

layer_words:spin_words.comment: A Spin found, and that it stays: the first also how they are found, one deeper in each dive. What a Spin does, and L and R, are BN6's own, unsaid (the voice sweep, docs/voice/sweep/net.md).
layer_words:spin_words.header: What a Spin of `colour` does, and that it stays (`first`: the profile's first, how they are found too): MegaMan's script, in `text`

layer_words:vendor_words.comment: The NaviCust vendor's greeting, naming the programs MegaMan has used in earlier runs that lead his list (`names`, n of them)

liberation_battle_words:lib_surrounded_w.header: Into `c` the battle's field where BN5 surrounds the Navi ("" else)

reward_words:draft_menu.comment: The draft: one box, the BugFrags of none in it, then the programs in a column with their colours and the copies held (ts_option: its number and those above and below it), each to its branch (`take`), B to `skip`. Its script. A box each said what BN6's programs do: seventeen boxes from the data to the pick, which the owner found far too many (6 October 2026).

reward_words:draft_take.comment: the draft's branches: a program given, or BugFrags for none; each sets `taken_flag` and ends, or goes on to the way on (`next`). A program that fits the board as it stands (its `fit_flag` set) is installed as it comes; else MegaMan says one moves first (the draft offers only programs that fit once they move): said after the pick, a plan, where three boxes before the menu said it of each (the owner, 6 October 2026: the reward's words were far too many)

reward_words:pick_three.comment: Three chips, one to take (event flag `flag` set as it is, after which `empty` is said instead); B leaves them (`leave`): a vault's, an official gate's. A pick is asked once more, "`verb` TrplShot J?", on No, which comes back to the three: a playtester's A pressed through the words before them took the first, for good (session 55).

reward_words:reward_items.comment: A guardian's HPMemory, his chip and the heal, in BN6's own boxes: what was given, and the heal; nothing of the Pack and the Folder, BN6's own (a playtester counted fourteen calls from a guardian's last words to the way on, session 63). The run's last gives only his chip: no HP or heal for a walk to its exit (a playtester given five HPMemory and a program after the final fight), and it stays in the Library.

flags.beats: three sentences or more in one box: one beat a box
flags.box-words: more than twelve words in one box: one beat a box, six words is normal
flags.button: a button or control named: BN6 names one once, at its first use, by whoever needs it
flags.colon: a colon in speech: the summary voice
flags.comma-space: a space after a comma: BN6 writes Lan,look!
flags.dash: a dash in speech: the summary voice
flags.direction-hyphen: a direction with a hyphen ("down-left"): directions are words, "to the lower left"
flags.glue: a formal glue word (however, additionally, therefore, in order to, currently...): BN6 says But, So, And
flags.hedge: hedging ("it seems that", "you might want to"): BN6's people say it straight
flags.line-long: a line broken by hand runs past twenty characters, so the box wraps it again
flags.long-speech: more than three boxes in a row from one speaker
flags.meta: a meta word (saving, game over, a run, checkpoint, level up, stats): nobody in BN6 knows the game is a game
flags.pages: pages on: the box wraps past three lines of twenty characters
flags.rule-talk: rule talk ("this layer", "this run", "the player"): characters speak in their world
flags.screen-talk: explaining the screen ("you can see", "on the screen")
flags.semicolon: a semicolon in speech: the summary voice
flags.spelling: a name not written as BN6 writes it
flags.summary: "which" or "whose" joining facts: the summary voice
flags.the-net: "the net" without its capital: BN6 writes the Net
flags.word-long: a word (or words joined by commas) past twenty characters, which the box cuts

sweep.text: Lan,{off} isn't on our board!{stands}{turns}{turns}{code_words}
sweep.why: The bare reminder after the PET: see off_board_note.

sweep.text: Lan! Chaud's clearance comes with the TagChip system! / Press SELECT in the Folder's EDIT, / then pick Choose TagChip. / Two tagged chips come to our hand together. / As long as they total under 60 MB!
sweep.why: Box 1 kept: the system the run gates behind Chaud's clearance belongs in his mail (as the Aquarium Director's TagChip mail in BN6), not MegaMan's mouth.

sweep.text: {about}'s compressed,Lan! / Dad's lab keeps its code for every dive now. / It's in his Compression mail!
sweep.why: "Dad's lab keeps its code for every dive now" is a rule across runs (1). The Compression mail is the place; a new-mail notice would do.

sweep.text: We've got battle data on him! / {tip}
sweep.why: Strategy (BN6 puts it on the BBS). Kept: Dad's battle-data mail covers BN6's guardians only, so this is the one place BN5's guardians' and the super bosses' tips are spoken since the story sweep cut MegaMan's tip before each guardian. Move them to BBS posts.

sweep.text: Lan,{off} is still off our board!
sweep.why: BN6 never reminds; a program off the board is the player's to see. If the reminder is wanted, the NaviCust's mail, once.

sweep.text: Lan,{off} isn't on our NaviCust board yet! / {turns}{turns}{turns}
sweep.why: As above.

sweep.text: Lan,a program isn't on our NaviCust board yet!
sweep.why: As above.

sweep.text: Layer {depth},Lan. We're in {area}!
sweep.why: "Layer N" repeats the arrival card's label, a level counter (rule 1, 6). "We're in {area}!" alone is the goal line.

sweep.text: Hold SELECT for a map of where we've been!
sweep.why: Names SELECT for the run's map on layers 1-2 until held (per session: every session hears it again). Rule 2 says once: a profile flag, or the second screen's legend.

sweep.text: Huh? Some of our chips came from the older Net... / Lan: And its cartridge isn't here! / Right. They'll sit out until it's back!
sweep.why: "And its cartridge isn't here!" is Lan knowing the ROM (1). The player needs it after a CONTINUE without BN5: a screen's notice (the title or the ROMs screen), not Lan.

sweep.text: Lan,look! A Spin for {c} programs! / Now we can turn {c} programs on the NaviCust! / Hold one,then press L or R. / And it stays with us,in every dive! / Each dive hides one more,deeper in. / A color we don't have yet!
sweep.where: Each dive hides one more,deeper in." is the run's meta (1). The Spin's mail, or the BBS.
sweep.why: "And it stays with us,in every dive!

sweep.text: {met}I busted {count} here in {sec}:{sec}.{cs}. / Beat that{rung}. / Real viruses,Lan! / If they delete us,the dive's over. / Let's heal up first if we're hurt.
sweep.why: "If they delete us,the dive's over." knows the run ends (1); kept and noted as the story sweep did in duel_words.

sweep.text: Lan,look! A ScrtData! / Three open the golden gate to the Secret Area. / It stands in the Undernet's copy. / A dark warp leads there. / Let's find two more!
sweep.why: The run's ScrtData system (three open the gate, where it stands) told by MegaMan at the pickup: a mail, or a Mr.Prog at the gate (rule 4). The third's goal line can stay.

sweep.text: Our second ScrtData! / One more,and the Secret Area's gate opens! / It's in the Undernet's copy!
sweep.why: As above.

sweep.text: Program data,too! Pick one! Or B for {skip_frags} BugFrags,Lan!
sweep.why: B named before the menu ("Or B for 30 BugFrags"); its choice, so kept. A legend in the menu itself would do it (rule 2).

sweep.text: It's sealed with {navi}'s code,Lan. / If we delete {navi} {needed} as a guardian... / ...in any dive,it'd crack! {beaten}
sweep.why: "...in any dive,it'd crack!" is a rule across runs (1). The gate's rule, by a Mr.Prog posted at it (rule 4), or a mail.

sweep.text: A vault,Lan! With a collector's lock. / It opens for a Library of {need} chips. / Ours has {have}. / Every chip we get counts,from any dive!
sweep.why: "Every chip we get counts,from any dive!" (1); the lock's rule, as above.

sweep.text: An official gate,Lan! / It needs Chaud's full clearance. / The official vault's behind it. Three Mega chips! / That takes three duel wins against ProtoMan. / The last is a NetBattle with him. We have {won}.
sweep.why: Chaud's clearance system recited at the gate (three duel wins, the last a NetBattle, "We have 2"): Chaud's mail's, or his call's (rule 4).

sweep.text: An official gate,Lan! / It needs Chaud's first clearance. / A Chip Order's behind it. Three chips we've held! / We get to order one. / One duel win against ProtoMan opens it. / Not yet,though!
sweep.why: As above.

sweep.text: L-Lan... That flame is dark data! / There's a DarkChip in it. {chip}!{bar}{does} / It only comes when I'm worried. / At a quarter HP,or hit again and again! / It's real power... But it eats at me. / Use one,and I go dark for that battle. / And each battle I use one in... / ...takes {DARK_PRICE} max HP,for this whole dive!
sweep.why: The price must come before the Yes, but six boxes are a lecture on a system the run adds. A Mr.Prog posted by the first flame, or Dad's mail on DarkChips, then one box at the flame.

sweep.text: L-Lan... That flame is dark data! / There's a DarkChip in it. {chip}! / Its darkness feeds on bugs! / Each use burns one of our BugFrags... / ...for {does}! / Then it bugs me,like a NaviCust bug. / For the rest of that battle! / No BugFrags? Then it's only {an} {base}. / And each battle it runs in... / ...takes {DARK_PRICE} max HP,for this whole dive!
sweep.why: As above: ten boxes on the run's BN6 DarkChip rule (BugFrags, bug, base chip, price).

sweep.text: |@M Lan,remember... {when} (the tip's last box, "strike while his lightning falls!", before every known guardian's battle call)
sweep.why: Rule 5: MegaMan coaching at the fight. The tip stays in Dad's mail, the briefing and the second screen

sweep.text: |@M Lan,remember... {when} (Bass's and the Cybeast's)
sweep.why: Rule 5, as the guardians'

sweep.text: @M {guardian_tip(11)}: ProtoMan's whole tip, five boxes, recited by MegaMan between ProtoMan's challenge and "Take the duel?"
sweep.why: Rule 5. His tells are BN6's own ProtoMan's (rule 3), and Dad's mail holds them once his copy is fought. The rest of the line is noted below

sweep.text: |@M His Soul,Lan! It's with us every battle. (every Soul after the first)
sweep.why: Rule 4: a power is taught once (the first Soul's words still do); the narration "MegaMan got: KnightMan's Soul!!" before it already says it

sweep.text: |@M And its battle data!|@M Next time,we'll know how it fights!
sweep.why: Rule 5: explains the run's battle-data system; the briefing simply knows the Cybeast next time. The guardians' same line was cut earlier (guardian_objs.c)

sweep.text: |@M And his battle data,Lan!|@M Next time,we'll know how he fights!
sweep.why: As above, for Bass

sweep.text: @C Tag two chips with SELECT in your Folder's EDIT.|@C They'll come to your hand together.|@C As long as they total under 60 MB.
sweep.why: Rules 2 and 3: BN6's own TagChip system (its key item, its EDIT entry) and a button. Chaud still names it: "And a NetBattler's trick. The TagChip system."

sweep.text: In the NaviCust,hold RIGHT on a program. Then press its code. (the Compression mail's second page)
sweep.why: Rules 2 and 3: BN6's own compression codes and a button; the mail comes only after the player has entered one

sweep.text: MegaMan's battle data, four or five boxes a guardian: "His fire tower gives no yellow warning!|It turns into our row. Sidestep it late!|..."
sweep.where: Strategy is the BBS's, in its posters' voices (rule 4), or a guardian's mail as the lab's data, not MegaMan coaching (rule 5). Two boxes coach outright: "Heal up before we face him!" (EraseMan), "Keep a Recover chip ready!" (DustMan)
sweep.why: The tells playtesters were deleted by unwarned (EraseMan's erase at low HP, CircusMan's tent, ProtoMan's lone panel); shown in the briefing, Dad's mail and the second screen

sweep.text: The same for Bass and the Cybeast ("His cape stops our shots cold!|...")
sweep.where: As above; they have no mail (Dad's are for BN6's guardians 1-18), so the BBS
sweep.why: As above

sweep.text: @M If he deletes us,our dive's over!|@L We can still run if it goes bad.
sweep.where: The stake as feeling, not as the run's end said aloud (rule 1: "our dive's over" is game over in the world's words): "He's not holding back,Lan!". `layer_words.c`'s `duel_terms` says the same for the races ("If they delete us,the dive's over.")
sweep.why: That the netbattle is a real fight (a playtester took it at 100 HP) and that running is allowed (a loss, not deleted)

sweep.text: |@M Pick {a Fire} chip last,like {HeatSht}. / |@M Pick {a Fire} chip last. / |@M Then UNITE! Once a battle.
sweep.where: Rule 4: a system by mail from whoever provides it (as BN6's NaviCust Support Center mails), or a power by whoever gave it; not MegaMan explaining the screen (rule 5)
sweep.why: How BN5's Soul Unison works in BN6's Custom Screen, the run's own; said once, at the first Soul

sweep.text: |@M A Soul or a Cross,though. Not both!
sweep.where: As above: the Soul mail; the second screen's card says it too
sweep.why: The run's rule that a Soul and a Cross are not worn together, said once a profile

sweep.text: Dad's report: " and HeatCross.\fIn it,fire chips +50,Buster +1.\fAqua attacks do double to it,and break it."
sweep.where: Rule 3: BN6's own Cross rules, taught in BN6's own Cross tutorials. A menu outside the fiction: the setup screen where the Cross is chosen, in its own plain style
sweep.why: What the brought Cross gives and fears (a playtester chose by weakness alone; three met EraseCross's erase unexplained)

boxes.text:
# smooth_motion: the game runs at the GBA's 60 frames a second. A 90, 144
# or 165 Hz screen shows each frame for one refresh or two (or two or
# three) in turn, which reads as judder. on mixes the two latest frames at
# every refresh, so motion is even, a little blurred and a frame later;
# off shows the game's own frames, sharp (best on 60 and 120 Hz). Options'
# Display changes it too.
